Suspicious inbound and outbound connections should be blocked at the firewall, router, access control list, or software-defined network policy layer. Exposed management services that are not required for investigation should be disabled, and any necessary remote administration should be restricted to a trusted management workstation. Automation rules, cloud integrations, and device-to-device control paths that could allow the compromised endpoint to influence other devices should be suspended. 3. Disable compromised credentials, administrative accounts, service accounts, API tokens, and remote access sessions that may be involved.
4. Block suspicious command-and-control, file-transfer, remote-administration, and lateral-movement traffic.
